newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo head quits in Swedish industrial shake-up.
newsitem.headline: Volvo head quits in Swedish industrial shake-up.

text.p: Swedish corporate life was rocked on Monday by a major shake out in which the boss of vehicle maker Volvo quit to be replaced by the dynamic head of appliance maker Electrolux.

Soren Gyll's decision to quit came as a shock, although he had indicated earlier he would retire before too long after five years at the helm of the car, truck and bus maker and he was forced to deny reports last year that he was at odds with company chairman Bert-Olof Svanholm.
Leif Johansson, 45-year-old Electrolux head, takes over at Volvo, leaving the empire of the Wallenberg family, Sweden's powerful business dynasty which holds a major chunk of Electrolux.

Johansson is replaced by Michael Treschow as president and chief executive. Treschow is presently president and chief executive of construction and mining equipment company Atlas Copco, another firm in the Wallenberg sphere of influence.
Italian Giulio Mazzalupi, a senior Atlas Copco executive, becomes the first non-Swedish chief executive of the construction company, Atlas Copco said in a statement.

Svanholm said Gyll would remain on the board of Volvo. Gyll took over Volvo in the wreckage of a failed marraige with French carmaker Renault, selling off most non-core assets to concentrate on the tough world of making cars and trucks.
Analaysts said Gyll's role was now seen to have been fulfilled and a dynamic figure was now needed to drive flat Volvo sales upwards in international markets.
Volvo said Gyll informed the board that he wished to leave his executive position at the annual general meeting of the company on April 23.
Gyll said in a statement that Volvo's goal of becoming exclusively a transport equipment group had essentially been implemented and the group was strong, financially as well as product wise.
"The group now faces a number of important strategic and structural decisions that will have consequences extending far into the future and whose implementation will demand continuity," Gyll said.
"It is against this background and since I had, in any event, intended to relinquish my executive duties next year at age 58, that I consider this is the proper time to pass the baton.
His successor, Johansson, who was born in 1951, joined Electrolux in 1984 and has been president since 1991 and chief executive officer since 1994, the statement said.
